source: the frozen forecast in predictions-<review>.json against the post-rebalance companies.json
note: THE FORECAST IS READ, NEVER RECOMPUTED. Every verdict scored here was written before the review took effect. Only funds whose workbook moved between the two dates are treated as evidence of what changed — a fund that was not re-read says nothing, which is different from saying nothing changed.

priceWindow.note: MSCI used one of the business days in this window and does not say which

funds.note: eems was not re-downloaded for this review, so its membership after the rebalance is UNKNOWN. It is excluded from every comparison rather than assumed unchanged.

segmentRule: the newest file that names the company decides its segment; where the files share a date, the larger position by market value decides

entered.label: Entered the index
entered.detail: Outside MSCI India IMI before the review, a constituent after it.

exited.label: Left the index
exited.detail: A constituent before the review, outside MSCI India IMI after it.

migration-up.label: Migrated up
migration-up.detail: Moved from the Small Cap segment into Standard: small-cap funds sell, the EM ETF buys.

migration-down.label: Migrated down
migration-down.detail: Moved from Standard into Small Cap: the EM ETF sells, small-cap funds buy.

no-change.label: No segment change
no-change.detail: In the same segment before and after. Its weight may still have moved.

precision.label: Of the companies we flagged as moving, how many moved

recall.label: Of the companies that moved, how many we flagged

stable.label: No-change calls that held
stable.caveat: A universe that mostly does not move makes these nearly free. This figure is a true-negative rate, it will always look high, and it is not evidence the model works.

retrospective.label: What the rules as they stand today would have said about this review
retrospective.caveat: IN-SAMPLE, and not a track record. These rules were designed after this review was scored. No threshold in them was fitted to it — every ratio is MSCI's, cited to a page — but the choice of geometry was made knowing the answer. One review is still one data point.

sizeCutoffs.basis: full market cap, which is the quantity MSCI expresses a size-segment cutoff in (GIMI p. 28)

precision.label: Of the companies these rules would flag, how many moved

recall.label: Of the companies that moved, how many these rules would flag

changes: size decided on full market cap, with free float as a separate minimum (GIMI pp. 28, 30)
MSCI's asymmetric migration buffers, 2/3 out and 1.5x in (pp. 44-45)
cutoffs derived by rank against the observed constituent count, not by the coverage walk
retrospective.attribution: the desk's decision, taken after seeing one review's outcome. The RATIOS are MSCI's and are cited to a page; the rupee cutoffs they are applied to are ours, derived from the constituents the funds hold. No threshold was tuned to fit the 33 events.
